result: The sea looked different this morning, as if someone had repainted every horizon in silver and lavender. I stood on the pier with cold wind tugging at my sleeves, listening to waves slap against weathered stones. Nearby, a fisherman repaired a blue net, his hands moving with the calm certainty of long practice. He caught my eye and nodded, as though we shared an old secret. Beyond him, gulls circled above a tiny lighthouse, whose pale beam swept across the water like a slow searchlight. The whole scene felt borrowed from a story waiting to be written. I opened my notebook, but the first sentence refused to arrive. Words can be shy, too, especially when the world is offering so much. Instead, I drew the lighthouse, the fishing boat, and the curved line of the distant shore. Slowly, the blank page began to feel less empty. Perhaps that is what creativity asks of us: not certainty, but attention. Not a perfect plan, but a willingness to linger, observe, and let small details become doors. By noon, the light had sharpened, the net was mended, and my sketch looked like a map to somewhere I had not yet been. I closed the notebook and walked home along the beach, carrying the quiet satisfaction of having begun something, even without knowing where it might lead. Some mornings are not invitations to conquer the world, but gentle reminders that wonder is already here, waiting beside the ordinary, like sunlight trembling on water.
